ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior officers against the Financial Services Commission (FSC) sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated List, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFUI) watchlist. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and family members/close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any trigger event. Automated screening tools with fuzzy matching and name variation algorithms are mandatory. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years. Any positive hit triggers immediate suspension of incorporation and a suspicious transaction report (STR) to KoFUI.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registry (I-REG) of the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean script (Hangul). Foreign names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul. The name must include the legal form suffix '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa). Four-tier naming conventions: (1) uniqueness within the same registry district; (2) no misleading terms regarding business scope; (3) no prohibited or sensitive tokens; (4) compliance with public order and morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written objection with the head of the registry office within 14 days of the rejection notice. The objection must state the grounds for appeal and include supporting evidence, such as a prior use certificate or a trademark registration. The registry head must issue a decision within 30 days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the Seoul Administrative Court within 90 days of the decision. The appeal process is governed by the Administrative Litigation Act and the Commercial Registration Act. It is advisable to consult a Korean attorney to prepare the appeal and ensure compliance with procedural deadlines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally permissible for registration purposes under the Commercial Act, but for a cybersecurity SaaS company, the National Tax Service (NTS) and commercial banks often reject virtual office addresses for VAT registration and corporate bank account opening. The NTS requires a physical place of business where records are kept and where tax inspections can be conducted. Banks require a physical address for due diligence and to verify the company's operational substance. Therefore, a virtual office is not recommended; a physical office lease or a serviced office with a dedicated meeting room is advisable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) The registered office must be a real, accessible location; (2) The NTS may conduct unannounced inspections to verify business substance, especially for VAT and corporate income tax; (3) The registry office may verify the office address during the incorporation process; (4) Banks may conduct on-site visits for account opening. The likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection is moderate (30-50%) for a SaaS company with no physical assets, but increases if the company claims tax incentives or has high transaction volumes. Mitigation: maintain a physical office, keep business records on-site, and ensure a responsible person is present during business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288-317 governing corporate formation of a stock corporation (Chusik Hoesa), including Article 289 (contents of the articles of incorporation), Article 292 (notarization of the articles), Article 295 (obligation to pay the share subscription price), Article 317 (registration of incorporation), Article 382 (duties of directors), Article 397 (non-competition obligations), and Article 412 (statutory auditor), supplemented by the Commercial Registration Affairs Handling Rule and the Local Tax Act for registration license tax.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Seoul Central District Court Registration Office or the District Court Registration Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Stock Corporation (Hoesa Seolrip Deunggi Sincheong) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jung-gwan), share subscription certificate, payment confirmation certificate from the capital escrow bank, and organ appointment documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not require any statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the full subscription price for all subscribed shares must be paid in before incorporation registration, and the paid-in funds must be held in a blocked subscription escrow account at a commercial bank in Korea until the corporation is registered. For non-resident subscribers, foreign exchange and source-of-funds documentation is required. The registration license tax is computed with reference to the stated capital amount, so the actual official fee will vary; USD 215 is a conservative low-capital SaaS estimate including registration license tax, local education surtax, and court filing fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA

WHEREAS, the Corporation was established and registered with the competent District Court Registration Office in the Republic of Korea under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended) (the "Act"); and

WHEREAS, the subscribers have duly executed subscription certificates and have fully paid the aggregate subscription price for all issued shares into the designated capital subscription escrow account, satisfying Articles 295 and 302 of the Act; and

WHEREAS, the subscribers have lawfully elected the undersigned as initial directors and statutory auditor at the organizational general meeting, and all consent and acceptance forms have been received; and

WHEREAS, the Board considers it necessary to ratify the share capital subscription, authorize the opening and operation of banking accounts, adopt the registered office, and appoint the statutory officers of the Corporation in order to proceed with day-to-day operations, tax filings, and contracting.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. Ratification of Share Capital Subscription. The initial share capital subscription is hereby ratified, confirmed, and accepted. The Corporation's authorized share capital is [●] ordinary shares with paid-up capital of [●] Korean Won, and the issuance of shares to the subscribers listed in the subscription schedule is approved. The subscription proceeds shall remain blocked in the escrow account and may be released to the Corporation only after registration as required by the Act and applicable banking regulations.

2. Banking Authorization. [●] Bank is approved as the primary deposit and transaction bank of the Corporation. The Chief Executive Officer is authorized, together with the Chief Financial Officer, to open and maintain corporate accounts, sign account applications, execute funds transfer instructions, register the corporate seal, and complete all ancillary documents that the Bank may require. Dual control shall be maintained over online banking certificates and payment tokens.

3. Adoption of Registered Office. The registered office of the Corporation shall be located at [●], [●]-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea. The directors are directed to file the address statements with the competent District Court Registration Office and the National Tax Service and to update the business registration whenever the registered office changes.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. [Name] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] is appointed Statutory Auditor. Each officer shall exercise his or her duties with fiduciary care, comply with the duty of loyalty under Article 382 of the Act, refrain from competing with the Corporation under Article 397, and shall not enter self-dealing transactions unless authorized by the Board. The Chief Executive Officer is delegated the authority to execute contracts, make routine business decisions, engage personnel, and represent the Corporation before all government agencies.

5. General Corporate Housekeeping. The Corporate Secretary is directed to issue share certificates after registration, maintain the corporate ledger and board minutes, apply for the corporate certificate and electronic signature, and file business registration and withholding tax registrations with the National Tax Service. All lawful expenses, fees, notarial charges, registration taxes, and professional fees incurred in connection with this resolution are ratified and approved.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that any one of the authorized officers may execute all documents, deeds, or instruments necessary to carry out the intent and purpose of this resolution.

PASSED AND ADOPTED at [place] on [date], by the unanimous vote of the initial directors present, and certified by the Corporate Secretary as a true and complete record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Share Subscription Schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public in the district of the intended registered office, with preliminary corporate name confirmation obtained through the Commercial Registry Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the court system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must prepare and execute Articles of Incorporation containing the mandatory statutory elements under Article 289 of the Commercial Act: corporate name, corporate purpose, address of the registered office, total authorized shares, par value of shares, capital amount, methods of notice and advertisement, duration, and names of promoters. The corporate purpose must be drafted comprehensively to cover cloud vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, managed security operations, SaaS delivery, research and development, licensing, and all ancillary infosec consulting services. At least one promoter must have the signed and sealed articles notarized before a Korean notary public. For foreign promoters, passport copies, alien registration cards, or corporate registration extracts with apostille or consular legalization, and a power of attorney if a Korean legal scrivener is engaged, must be prepared. The share subscription schedule must allocate shares among promoters and record the number of shares subscribed by each person. If all shares are subscribed by the promoters at the incorporation stage, a public subscription procedure is not required. The notarized original articles must be retained and submitted to the registry at the registration stage.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation signed by all promoters
Corporate name confirmation record (name-use report) from the court registration portal
Passport or alien registration card of each promoter
Power of attorney and legal scrivener letter of engagement, if used
Proof of intended registered office (preliminary lease agreement or owner consent)
Share subscription schedule listing subscribers, share class, and number of shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or court portal identifies a defective clause, the promoters must amend the articles and re-notarize the corrected instrument; the statutory or port can typically be cured within 14 days. If the corporate name is refused because of confusion with an existing enterprise, a new name confirmation must be obtained and substituted before re-issuance of the notarized articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Full Payment of Share Subscription Price
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in Korea, including a foreign exchange bank approved for capital remittances by non-resident shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the articles are notarized, the promoters must open a temporary capital subscription escrow account in the name of the future corporation or of the promoters as a designated deposit account at a Korean commercial bank. Each subscriber must remit the full subscription price for his or her allocated shares, which must not be less than the par value per share, into the blocked account. For non-resident subscribers, the transfer must be labelled clearly as a Korean Won capital remittance for incorporation, accompanied by the subscriber's passport and any required foreign exchange declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The bank will issue a certificate of paid-in subscription deposit indicating the total amount held, the name of each depositor, and confirmation that the funds are blocked until presentation of the court-issued certificate of incorporation. This certificate is an essential attachment for the incorporation registration. The promoters must not issue share certificates before the completion of registration, and the escrow account may not be drawn down except by the registered representative director after legal formation.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreement or subscription certificate executed by each subscriber
Bank remittance instructions and wire transfer confirmation for non-resident subscribers
Foreign exchange purchase/sale or inward remittance declarations, if applicable
Passport and proof of source of funds for each foreign subscriber
Capital escrow account opening application and bank account resolution
Certificate of paid-in subscription deposit issued by the Korean bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening for anti-money-laundering review, provide a written breakdown of the intended business model, customer base, and ownership chain and submit supplementary source-of-funds evidence. If the wire transfer is returned due to missing remittance purpose, instruct the remitting bank to include the exact reference "capital deposit for Korean incorporation" and resend within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration of Incorporation at the Competent District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea, or the Internet Registration Office (IROS) electronic filing portal of the courts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After all subscription amounts are fully paid into the blocked escrow account and the initial directors and statutory auditor have been appointed by the organizational general meeting, the incorporation registration application must be submitted to the competent District Court Registration Office. The application must be accompanied by the notarized original Articles of Incorporation, the certificate of paid-in subscription deposit, reports of appointment and consent forms of the initial directors and statutory auditor, the statutory auditor's election statement, the corporate seal certificate, and all attachments required by the Commercial Registration Affairs Handling Rule. The registration officer will review the legal capacity of promoters, the validity of the shares, the adequacy of the paid-in capital certificate, and compliance with tax registration prerequisite declarations. Upon approval, the registration officer records the incorporation in the commercial register and issues a certificate of registration, which is the legal date of formation under Article 317 of the Commercial Act. Pre-incorporation contracts must be ratified by the board after this registration to be legally binding.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration using the court-issued prescribed form
Notarized original Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in subscription deposit from the capital escrow bank
Consent forms and acceptance certificates of each initial director and statutory auditor
Report of appointment of directors and auditor signed by the incorporators
Corporate seal creation certificate and report of seal impression
Power of attorney and identification of the legal scrivener or representative, if any
Registration license tax and court fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order or inquiry, the missing documents must be submitted through the Internet Registration Office or the registry counter within the statutory correction period, ordinarily two weeks. If the application is rejected for substantial non-compliance, the defects listed in the rejection order must be cured in full and a new registration application filed with corrected dossiers, which will normally take a further seven working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Insurance, and Corporate Operations Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service with jurisdiction over the registered office, plus the Ministry of Employment and Labor, National Pension Service, and National Health Insurance Service for employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month from receipt of the court certificate of incorporation, the representative director must apply for business registration through the HomeTax online portal of the National Tax Service. The district tax office will issue a corporate business registration certificate, which is required to obtain electronic tax invoices, VAT identification, and corporate income tax filing credentials. The company must register as a VAT taxpayer, as a corporate taxpayer, and as a withholding agent for employee payroll taxes. If any employee is engaged, the company must also complete registrations with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and the Ministry of Employment and Labor for employment insurance and industrial accident compensation insurance. For a pure ISIC 6201 SaaS cybersecurity company, no industrial operating licence is required, but the company should maintain standard cloud service agreements, cybersecurity liability insurance policies, and Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) compliance documentation for Korean customers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of commercial registration issued by the court
Certified copy of the registered Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate and certificate of representative director's seal impression
Proof of registered office (lease agreement or title deed)
Representative director's identification and alien registration card, if foreign
HomeTax business registration application (saeopja deungrokeu)
Employment contracts and payroll records for employee registration purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office flags a mismatch between the business registration address and the commercial register, submit a lease certificate and a director's declaration and request an address correction through HomeTax. Late filing penalties may be cured by voluntary disclosure within the statutory grace period and prompt payment of any minor penalty before an audit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable -- the entity will operate exclusively as an information security SaaS vendor under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541512 and does not perform physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No operating manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing permit is required under Korean industrial licensing law for cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration testing SaaS.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable -- the activity is not a listed project category under the Framework Act on Environmental Policy EIA screening provisions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable -- the SaaS activity is conducted from office and cloud data center environments; no Full EIA Report, Environmental Registration, or exemption certificate is required for the software service itself.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable -- zero process wastewater, zero volatile organic compound emissions, and zero hazardous waste from the core software activity. Any data center electricity consumption and electronic waste are controlled by the cloud provider's operating agreements and standard e-waste recycling obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the software activity itself; however, if a dedicated office is leased, the company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, register the workplace with the Ministry of Employment and Labor, and verify that the building maintains a valid fire safety inspection certificate issued by the National Fire Agency. The company should document emergency evacuation routes, fire extinguishers, electrical safety, and an employee emergency response plan. For a pure cybersecurity SaaS activity with no handling of hazardous substances, no special Civil Defense clearance is required. As a sector-level best practice, the company should also maintain information security management system certification (ISMS) or ISMS-P under the Information and Communications Network Act if it processes or provides security services concerning Korean personal information.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) in South Korea must first incorporate at the court registry (deung-gi) and register with the local tax office. Upon incorporation, the company automatically receives a corporate tax identification number (business registration number, sa-eop-ja-deung-rok-beon-ho) issued by the district tax office under the NTS HomeTax system. For a branch or domestic place of business of a foreign corporation without a separate local entity, the foreign corporation must register for a domestic business place number via HomeTax by submitting the foreign corporation certificate, articles of incorporation, and proof of local place of business. The representative must complete the application with the certificate of incorporation, bylaws, identity documents, and power of attorney where applicable; the NTS issues the registration number within a few business days. VAT registration is generally effected automatically as part of the business registration process, and the business registration number serves as the VAT identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (South Korea does not operate a check-the-box regime; a Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate tax on worldwide income. No hybrid mismatch elections are available under Korean domestic tax law beyond the general thin-capitalization and controlled-foreign-company rules.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration; however, all newly incorporated domestic entities are generally required to register for VAT at the time of business registration regardless of expected turnover, and foreign corporations with a domestic place of business must register from the date of commencement of business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea operates an e-invoice (electronic tax invoice) mandate through the HomeTax system. All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices via the NTS national e-invoice platform or an NTS-certified ERP/API integration for all B2B supplies. Real-time transmission is required; the NTS validates the digital invoice, assigns a unique invoice number, and applies anti-fraud digital stamping through the automated e-invoice enforcement system (national e-invoice system). Failure to issue or transmit e-invoices can trigger penalties, including non-deductibility of input VAT and administrative fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods exported from South Korea may be zero-rated for VAT upon compliance with export customs clearance requirements. Qualifying services, including information technology and cybersecurity SaaS services to non-resident customers, may also be zero-rated under the 'export of services' regime where the consideration is received in foreign currency and the services are supplied to a non-resident party; the place of supply rules deem services that are physically performed or used outside South Korea, or supplied to a non-resident who is not a Korean domestic business, as zero-rated export services. The SaaS vendor must maintain service contracts, evidence of the non-resident status of the customer, and records proving the foreign currency consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent foreign exchange receipt evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may audit export zero-rating claims and require full documentation to substantiate the export or deemed export. In cases of fraudulent or unverified zero-rating, the NTS will assess the unpaid VAT (10%) retroactively, plus additional charges of up to 40% of the unpaid tax depending on the degree of intentionality or negligence, and impose criminal penalties for fraudulent evasion under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Additionally, the unwarranted refund may be clawed back with statutory interest and the supplier's VAT registration may be subject to enhanced monitoring or suspension.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance (MOSF) acting as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized and highly convertible foreign exchange regime. The Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions such as trade in services, dividend remittances, royalties, and software subscription payments, subject to mandatory reporting through a domestic foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions are also largely liberalized, but require prior notification or regulatory filing depending on the nature and size of the transaction. Foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa is permitted without prior approval under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, provided the investor files a notification with a designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Strategy and Finance. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds, and exporters may retain foreign currency in approved foreign currency deposit accounts. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal for non-resident shareholders once audited earnings are confirmed and the applicable 22 percent corporate income tax plus 15.4 percent dividend withholding tax is settled. However, the bank must verify the source of funds, confirm the transaction purpose code, and ensure that the remittance is within the remittance schedule stated in the foreign investment report. For cybersecurity SaaS businesses, service-related software license payments qualify as current account receivables and remit freely upon presentation of the underlying contract, tax invoice, and Korean export logistics confirmation. Overall, convertibility is high but compliance with the foreign exchange information report system is non-negotiable for every cross-border wire and escrow release.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received within six months from the date of export declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. One extension of up to six months may be granted by the head of the designated foreign exchange bank based on commercial rationale. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into Korean won; exporters may retain the foreign currency in a foreign currency account, convert it at market rates, or use it directly for import settlements, provided the receipt is reported to the foreign exchange bank electronically.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: As of the current regulatory landscape, fintech EMIs and offshore digital banks are not legally permitted to provide full corporate banking, foreign exchange custody, or capital verification services to a Korean Chusik Hoesa. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act assigns foreign exchange administration duties exclusively to domestic licensed banks and registered foreign exchange institutions. Offshore EMIs may offer foreign-currency payment collection for SaaS subscriptions only if they partner with a licensed Korean payment gateway, but they cannot act as a substitute for a tier-one commercial bank account, escrow repository, or foreign exchange purpose-code reporting engine. Feasibility is therefore Low for treasury-critical functions such as equity injection escrow, FX conversion, and regulatory filings. These EMIs should be limited to auxiliary collection channels for merchant SaaS payments routed into the domestic operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa with non-resident directors or shareholders, physical in-branch appearance is generally required for at least one duly authorized director or attorney-in-fact during the initial corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening can be considered by tier-one banks if the corporate resolution, power of attorney, director identification, and corporate registration certificates are notarized, apostilled, and submitted with an authentic Korean translation. The authorized representative must nevertheless undergo a video-based interview and a wet-signature verification process at a Korean embassy or a notary public in the incorporating jurisdiction. Certain banks require the Korean-registered director to appear personally, while KEB Hana Bank and Shinhan Bank have shown more flexibility for qualified foreign technology companies with existing institutional investor references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident natural person with no Korean tax identification number and no verifiable domestic footprint, triggering heightened anti-money-laundering scrutiny under the Financial Transactions Reports Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the bank with the UBO passport certified by the issuing authority, an apostilled corporate registry extract and shareholders register of the direct parent entity, a notarized declaration of beneficial ownership, 12 months of personal and corporate bank statements showing genuine revenue sources, a legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming the UBO is neither a politically exposed person nor subject to sanctions, and a certified English translation of the Chusik Hoesa's sealed articles of incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The cybersecurity SaaS activity involves penetration testing and vulnerability scanning tools that may be misclassified as dual-use technology, creating a reputational and export-control concern for the bank's compliance committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the business classification certificate confirming ISIC 6201 and NAICS 541512, an ISMS-P certification from the Korea Internet and Security Agency for in-country operations, a factual product description limited to cloud vulnerability scanning, a no-export-control-letter from a designated technology law advisor, customer engagement contracts with non-sanctioned enterprise clients, and a corporate board resolution defining the restriction that offensive cyber tools are not distributed in accrual or through reseller agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A proposed inbound equity injection of more than USD 1 million into a newly formed Chusik Hoesa without initial capital or operating revenue resembles a shell-company layering pattern and triggers mandatory suspicious transaction reporting thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the foreign investment notification issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the source-of-funds breakdown from the shareholder bank account, audited financial statements of the investing entity, a board-approved capital injection resolution, a forward-looking cash flow forecast showing software subscription pipelines, and a written business fulfillment plan stipulating that the funds will be allocated to development milestones, AWS or Azure cloud infrastructure, and cybersecurity compliance staffing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stated cybersecurity SaaS business purpose and expected high-volume outbound payments to unknown subcontractors or foreign software resellers may be treated as a red flag for invoice-gaming and money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substantiate the account with a complete vendor due-diligence package for all material counterparties, including polished legal entity IDs, KYB certificates, prior master service agreements, itemized invoices with service descriptions, evidence of actual service delivery such as penetration test reports or cloud logs, and a treasury policy requiring that every outbound disbursement above a defined threshold be matched with an executed statement of work.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a non-resident investor injecting capital into the Korean Chusik Hoesa, the compliant routing is as follows: execute a foreign direct investment notification through a designated foreign exchange bank using the official Form for Investment Report, then transmit the equity contribution via SWIFT MT103 with the Korean FX purpose code for acquisition of stocks in a locally incorporated foreign-invested company. The remittance beneficiary must be the foreign-invested company's capital escrow account or temporary receipt account at the domestic tier-one bank. The bank issues a capital verification certificate only after the full inward remittance matches the declared investment amount and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting has been accepted by the Bank of Korea through the electronic system. The funds may then be moved into the operational won account for lawful expenditure. Any upstream loan or convertible note must be separately reported and cannot be commingled with share capital proceeds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and licensing disbursements for the cybersecurity SaaS operation should be cleared via standard international correspondment banking rails. For recurring software licensing fees and cloud infrastructure costs, SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers are appropriate, with each payment tagged with the correct import-of-services purpose code and supported by a Korean tax invoice and service contract. For larger professional services or co-development agreements above the agreed treasury threshold, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by the Korean bank and confirmed by an offshore bank can support settlement. Documentary collections on terms such as documents against payment are available to mitigate counterparty risk while avoiding the cash-pre-payment burden. All outbound wires must pass through the designated foreign exchange bank to preserve the audit trail and comply with the daily foreign exchange position reporting regulations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign exchange forward contracts with maturity dates matching the underlying SaaS subscription revenue or dividend remittance cash flow
Non-deliverable forward contracts transacted through a licensed Korean bank with a qualified non-resident counterparty for hedging overseas subsidiary exposure
Cross-currency swaps for switching the denomination of syndicated or institutional loan liabilities from Korean won to US dollars or vice versa
Currency options and participating forwards approved by the designated foreign exchange bank for trade-related exposure hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting (AGM) and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: N/A - not a government filing; minutes and financial statements must be retained at the registered office in the statutory minute book; for listed companies only, disclosure to the Financial Supervisory Service via DART is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM does not trigger automatic strike-off, but shareholders, auditors, or the court can compel convening; directors are subject to administrative fines up to KRW 5 million; resolutions passed in a non-compliant AGM may be void or rescindable and directors may incur civil damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; one-month extension to April 30 is available for eligible corporations when the return is prepared and endorsed by a licensed Korean tax accountant or CPA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surtax equal to 20% of the tax assessed (reduced to 10% if filed within six months after the statutory deadline), under-reported tax surtax of 10%-40%, daily late-payment interest arising from the day after the due date, tax seizure and business registration closure by the NTS, and criminal liability for directors under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for fraudulent or repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the registered head office (Metropolitan City/Do or Si/Gun/Gu) via WETAX electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment local tax surcharge of 3% for the first month and 0.75% for each additional month up to a statutory maximum, plus daily delinquency interest; enforced collection through local tax seizure; issuance of a tax clearance failure certificate which can suspend transactions, licenses, and government tender participation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor's report and audited financial statements filing (only when audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after receipt of the external auditor's report and in all cases before the AGM approving the annual financial statements; the AGM itself must occur by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing of the required audit report exposes directors to administrative fines up to KRW 30 million; false or negligent audit reports may trigger criminal prosecution under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; persistent failure to appoint an auditor can lead to appointment by the FSS and legal sanction against directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business management report of a foreign-invested company (only if the company is classified as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing is subject to an administrative fine up to KRW 5 million; repeated non-compliance can result in revocation of foreign-invested enterprise status, loss of FIPA tax incentives, and restricted access to foreign exchange or capital account treatment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a compulsory independent CPA audit is legally required if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, the corporation has total assets of KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million) or more, or total liabilities of KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.3 million) or more, or annual revenue of KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million) or more; alternatively, mandatory audit is triggered if the company has 300 or more average full-time-equivalent employees. Listed companies, financial institutions, insurance/securities companies, public-interest corporations designated by Presidential Decree, and companies otherwise regulated under the Financial Services Commission are subject to audit regardless of size. For companies meeting these triggers, the audit must be performed by an independent Korean registered CPA firm, and the resulting audited financial statements must be filed with the FSS and presented at the AGM.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, the Korean-language text of IFRS approved by the Financial Services Commission) is mandatory for listed and public-interest companies; non-listed non-public companies subject to external audit may elect K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Standards, including the General Corporate Accounting Standards and SME Accounting Standards) unless required under K-IFRS by consolidation or statutory designation. The accounting framework elected must be consistently applied and disclosed in the notes to the financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not impose an annual UBO confirmation return on an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial-ownership information is maintained under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information; the company must keep and supply ownership and control data to financial institutions, counterparties, or KoFIU upon lawful request. Share transfers are recorded in the company's register of members and become effective vis-a-vis the company when the transfer is entered in that register. If the company is a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any change in ownership structure, including a foreign shareholding transfer or issuance of shares, must be reported to MOTIE through KOTRA within 30 days after the change; there is no annual UBO filing fee.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 1,800 per annum for a standard non-listed cybersecurity SaaS Chusik Hoesa (registered office location, corporate secretarial agent, AGM administration, statutory book maintenance, and tax-filing support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a mandatory K-IFRS/K-GAAP audit of a small or mid-sized Korean cybersecurity SaaS company; voluntary audit of a company below the statutory threshold may cost USD 5,000 - USD 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge, producing a combined top marginal rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives include: (i) R&D tax credit up to 30%-50% of qualifying cybersecurity research and cloud engineering expenditure; (ii) tax exemption or reduction for income from high-tech and new-growth-engine technologies; (iii) five-year corporate tax holiday in foreign direct investment zones and innovation hubs; (iv) special investment tax credits for industrial automation and digital infrastructure; and (v) for eligible venture or start-up companies, a 50%-100% reduction of corporate income tax on the first KRW 100 million of taxable income for up to five years. Tax credit and deduction stacking is capped and requires proper Korean payroll and actual business substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return per Article 40 of the Korean Corporate Tax Act, submitted through the National Tax Service electronic portal HomeTax at hometax.go.kr, with attached financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, and transfer-pricing disclosures.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with two statutory semi-annual interim prepayment returns for corporations with prior-year corporate tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within 3 months from the fiscal year-end, being 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year-end. A one-month extension may be available for audited subsidiaries with approved accounting reasons; late filings are not eligible for automatic grace days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number and corporate identifiers of the Chusik Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure the Korean company obtains a valid 10-digit business registration from the NTS before the filing deadline, and appoint a tax representative if no permanent establishment personnel are present in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year, legal name, and registered address in the Korean Commercial Registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact English name and address shown on the Tax Residence Certificate of the ultimate beneficial owner for treaty application consistency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Korean Standard Industrial Classification code and principal business description, namely cybersecurity SaaS, vulnerability scanning, and penetration testing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify as 6201 or 6209 regardless of where servers are hosted; Korean-source subscription revenue cannot be re-characterized as pure export merely because payment is collected through Stripe or a foreign acquiring bank.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue reconciliation, including SaaS subscription, licensing, implementation services, reseller margins, and support fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue where the Korean entity carries out value creation; cross-border intercompany revenue must follow arm's length pricing and be supported by contracts, invoices, and bank receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income and exempt income adjustments, including dividend income and foreign-source income claimed for foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean-resident corporation is taxed on worldwide income; attach the foreign tax credit form rather than a bare foreign declaration, and verify that dividend income qualifies for relevant exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expense calculation and disallowance adjustments for entertainment, donations, non-business expenses, and intercompany charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid to foreign affiliates for cloud infrastructure, security research, and SaaS platform licensing are deductible only if arm's length and evidenced by a transfer-pricing study; technical service fees may also trigger source-country withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base and applicable progressive corporate tax rate band.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%, 19%, 21%, or 24% national rate bands after adjustment; no treaty directly reduces the corporate income tax computation of the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated corporate income tax, advance payments, withholding credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that foreign tax credits are supported by foreign assessment notices; any under-withholding on distributions to non-resident shareholders must be separately reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge payable at 10% of national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local surcharge is not covered by most income tax treaties and remains payable even when the national tax is reduced by treaty credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International related-party transaction schedule, transfer-pricing documentation status, and controlled foreign company disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory where cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 500 million; attach Local File and Master File when statutory thresholds are met, supported by a Korean-translated transfer-pricing report.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and defective filing expose the corporation to: (i) a non-filing negligence tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; (ii) an under-reporting penalty of 10% of the deficient tax, or 40% where the shortfall is fraudulent; (iii) late-payment delinquency surcharges, comprising 3% of the unpaid amount for the first month and 0.75% for each later month or part thereof; and (iv) administrative penalties for failure to submit transfer-pricing and international transaction schedules. A wholly non-filing entity with unpaid tax liability exposes directors to criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final withholding tax on dividends paid by a Chusik Hoesa to a non-resident corporate shareholder, plus 2% local income tax surcharge, being 10% of the national withholding tax, producing a combined statutory withholding burden of 22% before treaty application.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement, the non-resident corporate shareholder must submit a Tax Residence Certificate issued by its foreign fiscal authority to the Korean payer or the NTS, together with a beneficial ownership declaration, corporate register excerpt, and the treaty relief application form prescribed by NTS. The application must be lodged before or at the time of dividend distribution; NTS issues a treaty withholding reduction or refund determination; retroactive relief may be pursued through a correction return within the statutory claims window.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local surtax, aggregating 22%, on IP royalties and debt interest paid to non-resident related companies. Under Korea's principal OECD-based double taxation agreements, treaty withholding is generally reduced to 10%-15% for royalties and interest, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and satisfies limitation-of-benefits conditions; dividends from substantial shareholdings are commonly reduced to 5%-10%, and portfolio dividends to 15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions for the fiscal year exceed KRW 5,000,000,000; Master File is additionally required when the Korean entity's annual revenue exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000 or foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 50,000,000,000; an international transaction summary schedule is triggered at KRW 500,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korean law does not operate an UAE-style standalone ESR register, but economic substance is enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule, substance-over-form jurisprudence, controlled foreign corporation rules, and beneficial ownership requirements in Korean tax treaties. A cybersecurity SaaS Chusik Hoesa must maintain Korean premises, an operating board, risk-bearing capital, original data and contracts, and actual cybersecurity engineers; outsourced SaaS functions booked in a low-tax affiliate without real management authority will be recharacterized, treaty relief denied, and royalties disallowed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting SaaS subscription and penetration-testing revenue received through Stripe or wire transfers, creating counterfeit invoices and expense vouchers, or shifting revenue to personal nominee accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal referral under the Korean Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, yielding imprisonment and fines up to multiples of the evaded tax; civil assessments include a 20% non-filing penalty and a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty on the deficient tax, plus late-payment surcharges and accrued interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or approve fraudulent invoices become jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax under the responsible-party rule; personal bank accounts, real estate, and overseas assets may be seized, departures from Korea may be blocked by travel bans, and egregious cases lead to imprisonment.
